subject: Renewal: Priority Support Expansion & Latency SLO Addendum
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ross <elena@opalcloud.com>, Samir Patel <samir@opalcloud.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 14:02:00 -0000
Subject: Renewal: Priority Support Expansion & Latency SLO Addendum

Hi Elena / Samir —

Hope you're both doing well. Opal's renewal is coming up on June 15; congrats on the growth this year — your average tokens/sec has doubled and we want to make sure support and SLOs match that trajectory.

Attached is a short proposal that outlines:
- a premium support bucket (24/7 priority queue + named CS lead)
- a p99 latency SLO option for inference endpoints under a Dedicated reservation
- a sample runbook and rollback policy for latency breaches

High-level ask: if Opal is willing to move to a 12-month committed Dedicated pool (baseline 12k rps token-equivalent) we can offer the p99 SLO at 99.95% and a commercial discount tier. If you'd prefer to keep Hosted only, we can offer a slightly relaxed SLO and a credit-based remediation.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Quick sync (20m) this week to confirm the desired SLO band and capacity profile
2) Marcus to validate technical feasibility/ops impact
3) Procurement to confirm PO/term changes and DocuSign flow

I'm free Thursday or Friday afternoon PT. Attaching the initial draft SLO table and last quarter's usage export so you can see the baseline.

[Attachment: priority_slo_proposal.pdf (6 pages)]
[Attachment: opal_usage_q1_2028.csv]

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

Date: Wed, 02 May 2028 09:18:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Priority Support Expansion & Latency SLO Addendum

Thanks Avery — appreciate the note and the clear options. A couple of clarifying questions before we sync: 
- Can you confirm whether the p99 99.95% SLO requires Dedicated or if it's supported on Hosted with guardrails?
- For the Dedicated baseline you called out (12k rps token-equivalent) — how did you size that against our peak 95th percentile from Q1? Is burst capacity included?
- On pricing: Samir and I are looking for a blended discount if we do 12 months + a 20% uplift in committed spend.

We're good to do a 20m call Friday 10:00am PT — Samir and I will book it. Procurement (cc'd) will want an explicit list of deliverables tied to the term changes.

Best,
Elena
VP Product, Opal Cloud
elena@opalcloud.com

Subject: Re: Renewal: Priority Support Expansion & Latency SLO Addendum (internal)

Avery — quick internal note ahead of the call.

- Dedicated required for consistent p99 99.95% at Opal's current model mix. Hosted could get you ~99.7% p99 under steady load but tail risks at peak (multi-tenant scheduling).
- Sizing: 12k token-rps baseline maps to ~3 x n1-gpu pools with our current kernel set; that covers 95th percentile plus 20% headroom for bursts. Burst capacity can be configured but billed as on-demand (we can include a 72-hour burst credit in the term if needed).
- Ops impact: Need a named on-call engineer during business hours + weekly SLA review for first 90 days. Grace can propose a runbook snippet.

I'll be on the call Friday; will bring a short slide on latency profiling.

—Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
From: Samir Patel <samir@opalcloud.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Ross <elena@opalcloud.com>
Cc: procurement@opalcloud.com
Date: Wed, 02 May 2028 15:45:27 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Priority Support Expansion & Latency SLO Addendum

Avery / Elena — thanks for the proposal. A few concrete asks from Opal: 
1) We are prepared to commit to 12 months if Redwood will: 
   - Guarantee p99 <= 120ms for our primary inference endpoint (us-west) at 99.95% over a monthly window
   - Provide a dedicated customer success engineer and 24/7 priority queue access
   - Include up to 10% burst capacity per month at the committed rate; anything above billed at on-demand rates
2) Commercial: we want a single-line discount applied across both compute and support (target ~20% off list if committed).
3) Contract: procurement prefers a DocuSign route, and they'll need a short SLA addendum that calls out credits and remediation steps (not full SOC language, just SLOs + credit table).

If Redwood can accept items 1-3, we'll advance to signature this month.

Samir
Head of Platform Ops, Opal Cloud
samir@opalcloud.com
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal: Priority Support Expansion & Latency SLO Addendum

Elena / Samir / Procurement — thanks for the clear asks and for confirming the Friday sync. Quick recap and agreed next steps: 

Recap of what Redwood will deliver if Opal signs a 12-month Dedicated commitment:
- SLO: p99 <= 120ms (us-west inference endpoint), monthly window; SLO target 99.95%
- Support: named CSM + 24/7 priority queue routing; weekly SLA review for 90 days then monthly
- Capacity: baseline Dedicated pool sized to 12k token-rps with 10% monthly burst included at committed rates; additional burst billed on-demand
- Ops: 72-hour burst credit on first month to smooth migration; runbook + on-call handoff included
- Commercial: 18% blended discount applied across compute + support (we can increase to 20% if Opal agrees to a 24-month term)

Attachments: updated SLO table with credit tiers and a one-page exhibit for the DocuSign packet.

Action items:
- Avery to upload the one-page SLA exhibit to DocuSign and share link (by EOD Friday) — https://www.docusign.com/sign/REQ-OPAL-72
- Opal procurement to confirm billing entity and PO cadence
- Marcus and Grace to finalize runbook snippet and on-call roster for the kick-off

[Attachment: priority_slo_proposal.pdf (updated v2)]
[Attachment: opal_usage_q1_2028.csv]

If that all looks right, I'll send the DocuSign package and a short amendment for signature.

Thanks — talk shortly on the call.

Best,
